title: Cap. VIII Arg. 9 (Thomas of Argentina): adult reprobation from foresight of final bad use of free will
pass_a_gloss: From the ancient Scholastics Thomas of Argentina confesses that he deserts the common opinion of the Theologians, and tries against them to prove this conclusion, That the cause of reprobation as to adults is the evil use of free will, about to last in them unto the end of life, foresighted from eternity by God. Which opinion differs in words, not in sense, from the Jesuit and Arminian. Let us therefore hear the reasons of Argentina.
pass_b_english: Among the older Scholastics, Thomas of Argentina admits he deserts the common opinion of the theologians, and tries against them to prove this: that the cause of reprobation as to adults is the evil use of free will lasting in them to life's end, foresighted by God from eternity. That opinion differs in words, not in sense, from the Jesuit and Arminian. Let us hear Argentina's reasons.
source_text: Ex antiquis Scholasticis Thomas de Argentina fatetur se communem opinionem Theologorum deserere, ac conatur contra eos hanc conclusionem probare, Causam reprobationis quoad adultos esse malum usum liberi arbitrii, usque ad finem vitae in ipsis duraturum, ab aeterno a Deo praescitum. Quae opinio verbis, non sensu, differt a Jesuitica et Arminiana. Audiamus igitur Argentinae rationes.
